answer: One concrete sybil defense is to require each agent identity to post a stake that is burned on misbehavior, much like cutting timber costs the forester real labor before any board is sold. An attacker spawning a raven flock of fake agents must lock capital in every one, so cost scales linearly while each fake identity earns little. Peers also attest only agents with verifiable work over time, so a new identity starts in a cold nebula with no trust and no earnings. Cheap creation becomes expensive influence, and the return on each fake identity turns negative before it can cash out.
